name: GM - Parma Metal Center, Parma OH

fieldNotes.site: GM Parma Metal Center, 5400 Chevrolet Blvd, Parma OH 44130 (Cleveland metro). 2.3M sq ft stamping/metal-assembly plant operating since 1948, just south of I-480 between W 130th St and Tiedeman Rd. Roster coords pointed at a residential area ~2.5 km N; relocated via satellite + web to the large light-roofed stamping complex at 41.41555,-81.77355. Building positively identified by its monolithic stamping-plant roof, west-side multi-track rail yard with railcars and spurs into the building, covered conveyor bridge across the south apron, and the 2-story brick administration building fronting Chevrolet Blvd on the east.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Whole property is enclosed by chain-link security fence - confirmed in 2024 Street View along the Chevrolet Blvd (north) frontage, where the fence runs the full building length with the metal-clad plant wall set back behind it. As a UAW/GM stamping plant, access is controlled; truck/rail entrances pinch through the fence line on the NW (rail-served material side) and a second on the south/SE. truckGate true.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Medium confidence. Standard for GM plants of this vintage and size to staff a guard booth at the main controlled gate; Street View does not have a pano at the interior truck entrances to image the booth directly, but the fenced, single-controlled-entry layout is consistent with a manned gate. guardShack true, remoteGs false. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 10-25 band. Covered dock/truck apron runs along the south face of the main building (z19 imagery shows a long covered dock canopy and a conveyor bridge); additional truck doors on the west face near the rail yard. Counted ~22 doors across south + west faces; flagged uncertain because much material moves by rail and some doors are under canopy.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: true - inbound steel arrives by rail and truck on the WEST/NW side (multi-track rail yard with coil cars, spurs into building); outbound stampings ship from truck docks on the SOUTH face. Two physically separate material faces.
fieldNotes.railServed: true - definitive. A multi-track rail yard with railcars (boxcars/coil cars) runs the full west edge of the plant with spurs entering the building (steel coil inbound). Clearly visible in z18 west-side imagery.
fieldNotes.dropYard: true - a band of drop trailers and material containers is staged along the south building face, plus marked trailer parking between the dock apron and the employee lot. dropArea 10-25.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 10-25 - rows of staged trailers/containers visible along the south apron in z18-z19 imagery, separate from the dock-active trailers.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: false - one integrated stamping + metal-assembly building. The separate building clusters immediately south (own parking) and the self-storage/RV-style building to the SE are NOT GM and are excluded. The administration block is attached to the main plant on the east.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~110 acres for the fenced GM perimeter (main plant, rail yard, dock aprons, drop staging, and employee parking). Derived from the perimeter polygon.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: ~45 estimate combining the south drop band and west material staging; flagged approximate.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban - dense Cleveland/Parma metro industrial fabric, adjacent residential and I-480.
fieldNotes.perimeter: Oriented ring traces the fenced GM property: NW corner at the rail yard, NE along Chevrolet Blvd past the office, south down the east employee-lot edge, SW across the south yard, and north up the west rail edge.
fieldNotes.truckGate box: NW rail-side controlled entrance off the Chevrolet Blvd corridor where the material/rail drive crosses the fence line.
fieldNotes.dockAprons: Two: a long thin strip along the south building face (primary outbound docks) and a strip on the west face beside the rail yard (inbound).

citations.claim: Nov 2025: GM commits ~$250M to Parma Metal Center to enable production of sheet-metal stampings and assemblies - active GM plant

verification.rationale: New GM-operated stamping plant (operating since 1948); survived the 2009 bankruptcy and received a fresh ~$250M investment in Nov 2025. Not a divested or RACER site.
